hidden_gems.name: Borghetto sul Mincio at the Visconteo bridge
hidden_gems.why: A mill village on a green river, not a lake selfie. One of I Borghi più belli d'Italia. With a newborn you can see the whole postcard in 20–30 minutes, then sit down.
hidden_gems.how_from_bardolino: South via Lazise/Peschiera or inland via Calmasino. About 25–30 minutes.
hidden_gems.parking_note: Park above the village or at the signed lots near the river; do not attempt the tiny lanes. Sigurtà lots work if you combine the two.
hidden_gems.stroller_note: Stone and short slopes to the mills; carrier for the last photogenic alleys, stroller fine on the upper paths.
hidden_gems.best_time: Arrive 09:15 or after 15:00. Skip Saturday lunch unless you booked.
hidden_gems.avoid_if: You only have energy for a harbor gelato — this is inland and worth the drive, not a filler.

hidden_gems.name: Cisano olive shore and Museo dell'Olio
hidden_gems.why: The quiet neighbor beach/olive strip when Bardolino harbor is loud. Use on rest days, not as one of the four trips.
hidden_gems.how_from_bardolino: 5–8 minutes south on the lake road, or a long stroller walk.
hidden_gems.parking_note: Small paid bays; if full, return to Bardolino lungolago lots.

hidden_gems.name: Castello Scaligero di Torri del Benaco (courtyard + small museum)
hidden_gems.why: The east-shore castle people actually enjoy with a baby: compact, lakeside, no peninsula traffic jam.
hidden_gems.how_from_bardolino: Best as a ferry hop from Bardolino/Garda. By car 20–25 minutes north, parking tighter in August.
hidden_gems.parking_note: Harbor lots fill; ferry avoids the problem.
hidden_gems.stroller_note: Piazzetta is easy; museum stairs are not. Courtyard is enough.
hidden_gems.best_time: Late morning ferry, lunch in town, early boat back.
hidden_gems.avoid_if: Bora-style wind days; boats get cancelled.

hidden_gems.name: Peschiera fortress canals at Fortezza
hidden_gems.why: Austrian star-fort, water on both sides, gelato, and a real lido. It photographs like a mini-Venice without 400 bridges.
hidden_gems.parking_note: Parcheggio Fortezza / lots near the walls. Easier than Sirmione by a wide margin.
hidden_gems.stroller_note: Flat walls and bridges with manageable ramps if you pick the main circuit.
hidden_gems.best_time: Morning for parking; swim after 11:00 if the baby is in shade.
hidden_gems.avoid_if: You expected a wild beach — this is a fortress town with lidos.

authentic_food.name: Tortellini di Valeggio
authentic_food.why: The dish to plan a day around. Broth or burro e salvia. Baby can sleep in the carrier while you eat a proper lunch.
authentic_food.best_time: Lunch sitting. Many kitchens rest on one weekday — check.
authentic_food.avoid_if: You only want a lake-view menu turistico.

authentic_food.name: Persico and coregone on the east shore
authentic_food.why: Order lake fish, not frozen sea prawns. Harbor fronts in Bardolino are mixed: walk one street inland for better value.
authentic_food.how_from_bardolino: On foot from the apartment for dinner after any day trip.
authentic_food.parking_note: N/A for evening in town; use the apartment.
authentic_food.stroller_note: Lungolago is the easiest stroll of the holiday.
authentic_food.best_time: Dinner back in Bardolino — you must be home anyway.
authentic_food.avoid_if: Laminated 12-language menus with photos of carbonara.

authentic_food.name: Olio extravergine and Bardolino Classico
authentic_food.why: Cantina Zeni / Museo del Vino is a rainy or rest-day move: short, indoor, stroller-possible, and you still sleep in your own bed.
authentic_food.best_time: A rest day or a storm.
authentic_food.avoid_if: The baby is overstimulated — keep it to 45 minutes.

less_crowded_alternatives.name: Skip Sirmione unless you win the 08:15 parking lottery
less_crowded_alternatives.why: The castle is real. The peninsula traffic and ZTL are also real. Peschiera gives water + walls + a swim without the Marconi queue.
less_crowded_alternatives.parking_note: Sirmione: Monte Baldo / Marconi fill by 10:00 in high season; Colombare is the honest backup with a long walk.
less_crowded_alternatives.stroller_note: Old town cobbles + crowds. Grotte di Catullo is a hike — do not.
less_crowded_alternatives.best_time: If you insist: arrive before 08:30, castle, coffee, leave by 13:00.
less_crowded_alternatives.avoid_if: August weekend, late start, or a baby who needs a feed in a crush.

less_crowded_alternatives.name: Torri del Benaco instead of Malcesine
less_crowded_alternatives.why: Malcesine is beautiful and packed; the cable car is a queue machine. Torri is the calmer castle-and-harbor town, and the ferry already goes there from Bardolino.
less_crowded_alternatives.avoid_if: You came specifically for Monte Baldo views — then Malcesine, but not with this infant plan.

scenic_spots.name: Punta San Vigilio and Baia delle Sirene
scenic_spots.why: The prettiest swimming corner of the east shore. Limited parking is the tax you pay. Better as a short add-on from Garda town than as a late arrival.
scenic_spots.how_from_bardolino: 10–15 minutes north, or ferry to Garda plus a short taxi/walk depending on energy.
scenic_spots.parking_note: Paid, fills, pedestrian underpass from the lot. Have a backup: swim at Cisano or Peschiera lido instead.
scenic_spots.stroller_note: Short walk from the lot; bay paths mixed. Carrier for pebbles.
scenic_spots.maps_query: Baia delle Sirene Punta San Vigilio parking

scenic_spots.name: Bardolino harbor at golden hour — after you are already home
scenic_spots.why: You do not need another town for a sunset. The 18:00 rule is a feature: gelato, lungolago, bed.

ferry_opportunities.name: Bardolino → Garda → Torri del Benaco → Bardolino
ferry_opportunities.why: The correct boat day for a six-month-old: two pretty harbors, a castle courtyard, lunch, home for a nap. Not the 4-hour slow boat to Riva.
ferry_opportunities.how_from_bardolino: Walk or 4-minute drive to Bardolino imbarcadero. Buy tickets 20 minutes early at the Navigazione Laghi window or app.
ferry_opportunities.parking_note: Leave the car at the apartment or the imbarcadero lots. This is the easiest parking day of the holiday.
ferry_opportunities.stroller_note: Carrier for boarding and swell. Fold stroller. Boats have steps/gaps.
ferry_opportunities.best_time: Late morning departure, back mid-afternoon. Check the seasonal PDF the night before.
ferry_opportunities.avoid_if: Wind warnings, sciopero, or a baby with ear pain (discuss with a doctor; lake boats are usually fine).

ferry_opportunities.name: Optional foot crossing Torri ↔ Maderno
ferry_opportunities.why: The car traghetto is the lake's only vehicle ferry. You do not need the car. As foot passengers it is a 30-minute scenery hop if the short loop felt too short and the timetable still gets you home.
ferry_opportunities.how_from_bardolino: Only after arriving in Torri by passenger boat. Do not drive the traghetto 'for fun' with a newborn unless you already planned a west-shore parking day.
ferry_opportunities.stroller_note: Vehicle deck is noisy; stay in passenger areas; carrier on.
ferry_opportunities.best_time: If the first Torri lunch ended early.
ferry_opportunities.avoid_if: Behind schedule. Never chase Maderno if the return Bardolino boat is the last sensible one.

tourist_traps.name: Sirmione at midday in high season
tourist_traps.why: You will spend the baby's good hours in a car queue and then pay €16–25 to walk into a crush.
tourist_traps.avoid_if: Always, for this family, unless scores somehow invert.

tourist_traps.name: Gardaland with a 6-month-old
tourist_traps.why: A theme park is noise, sun, and queues. It does not serve this baby.

tourist_traps.name: Photo menus on the Bardolino / Lazise piers
tourist_traps.why: Not dangerous, just sad. Walk inland one block.
tourist_traps.avoid_if: You like paying sea-fish prices for frozen product.

timing_rules: East-shore lake road (SR249) crawls in late morning high season. Leave before 09:00 for any car trip south.
Monday inland restaurants may close. Check Valeggio the night before.
Ferries: ticket office 20 minutes early. Seasonal timetables change in April/May and mid-October.
Venice: weekday only if you can choose. Weekend Santa Lucia is a harder stroller/carrier day.
Never schedule a 'sunset in another town.' You live in Bardolino. Use it.
baby_local_tips: Farmacie: look for the green cross; after hours the door lists the farmacia di turno.
Bardolino tourist medical studio (seasonal): Via Croce 35, typically morning hours, tel +39 045 511 7746 — confirm season dates at the comune.
Nearest hospital emergency pointer on the east shore: Ospedale Pederzoli, Peschiera del Garda.
Lungolago benches in Bardolino and Garda are the real feeding infrastructure.
Lake water is not a bathtub. For a 6-month-old, shade and a dip of feet beat a lido marathon.
rainy_local: Museo del Vino / Cantina Zeni, Bardolino — short, indoor, local.
Valeggio lunch + covered walks in town if Sigurtà is a wash (the park is still outdoor).
Peschiera has more arcades and cafe indoor seating than the pretty villages.
Verona is the nuclear rainy option — only if you accept cobbles and a carrier-only historic centre. Keep it to 4 hours and still be home before 18:00.
